status_note: First-authored 10-week overhead-mobility arc — the shoulder / thoracic / scap coordination needed to snatch, OHS, and press without shoulder pain. Evidence base drawn from whitepaper 04_handstand_walk.md and motor-learning literature (whitepaper 03), plus 4 shoulder-specific citations that need pre-launch URL verification.

goals.primary: Add ROM-under-load overhead — shoulder flexion, thoracic extension, scap upward rotation
goals.secondary: Reduce anterior-shoulder irritation risk during heavy overhead work (snatch, OHS, press)
explicit_non_goals: Building a snatch PR — mobility opens the door; technique + strength walks through it
Replacing a physio evaluation for actual shoulder pathology

principles.rule: Passive ROM before active ROM before loaded ROM.
principles.detail: Ludewig & Cook 2000 documented altered shoulder kinematics — scap upward rotation lagging shoulder flexion under load — in people with symptomatic shoulders. We build the kinematic pattern before we add weight.

principles.rule: Every drill card ships a Wulf-compliant external-focus cue.
principles.detail: Wulf 1998, 2013 — external focus outperforms internal for skill retention. `reach for the ceiling` beats `contract your lats`.

principles.rule: Scap upward-rotation drills come before shoulder-flexion drills in every session.
principles.detail: Ludewig & Reynolds 2009 — scap dyskinesis (upper-trap dominance) is the most consistently documented kinematic association with symptomatic shoulders in athletes — an association, and a contested one as a cause. Fix the sequence, not just the range.

principles.rule: No bouncing / rebound stretches at end-range shoulder flexion.
principles.detail: Engineering choice, not a cited finding — we ask for active rotator-cuff engagement before end-range positioning, because ballistic end-range loading is what that engagement is there to protect against. No retrieved text in Reinold et al. 2007 (J Athl Train 42(4):464-469, EMG in 22 asymptomatic subjects) or in the Reinold, Escamilla and Wilk 2009 review (JOSPT 39(2):105-117, Level of Evidence 5) states that activation must precede end-range loading.
Karni 1998, Walker 2003 consolidation — motor patterns consolidate with sleep between sessions. Short daily > long infrequent for mobility acquisition.

plan_tiers.label: Foundation — Wall-arm-raise fails / can't reach vertical
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 10: supine shoulder flexion 165-175°, empty-bar OHS to parallel without heel lift, first snatch-grip Sotts press.

plan_tiers.label: Progression — Vertical passive, loaded overhead is stiff
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: By week 10: 180° passive + loaded OHS at 50% BW to parallel, snatch-grip Sotts at bar weight for reps.

plan_tiers.label: Push — Vertical loaded, chasing efficiency + endurance
plan_tiers.typical_outcome: Overhead endurance (Turkish get-up hold ≥ 30s each side at 24kg), snatch balance to 60% snatch 1RM without sequencing errors.

questions.label: Realistically, how many days per week can you commit?
questions.help: Honest answer wins. If your ceiling is 2, we'll tell you upfront whether this program can deliver on its claim at that dose.

questions.label: Lie flat, arms overhead — how close can you get elbows to the floor?
Do you currently snatch, OHS, or press overhead?
Does anything hurt in the last 30 degrees of overhead reach?
Diagnosed rotator-cuff tear, or persistent rotator cuff-related shoulder pain (also called impingement)?
Shoulder dislocation or subluxation in the last 12 months?
Recent neck flare or radicular pain into the arm?
Has one shoulder lost range in ALL directions over weeks or months — including when someone else moves it for you?
questions.help: That pattern suggests adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder), which needs its own rehab protocol.

questions.label: Sharp, well-localised pain right on top of the shoulder, where the collarbone meets the shoulder blade?
questions.help: That's the AC joint. End-range overhead flexion can amplify an irritated one.

questions.label: I consent to storing training log + symptom scores.

consent.label: I understand this is training programming, not medical advice. Real shoulder pain goes to a physio.
I agree to stop the session if sharp shoulder pain appears during overhead work.

physical_tests.label: Supine shoulder flexion
physical_tests.instructions: Lie flat on your back, arms overhead. Have someone measure the angle between your upper arm and the floor. 180 = elbows touching floor. Ballpark is fine.

physical_tests.label: OHS depth (hip below knee)
physical_tests.instructions: Empty-bar overhead squat to the lowest position you can hold without heel lift or forward collapse. Measure how far your hip crease is BELOW the top of the knee. Positive = hip below knee. Zero = parallel.

physical_tests.label: Turkish get-up overhead hold
physical_tests.instructions: Get-up to the tall-sit or half-kneeling position with a KB (choose a challenging but controllable weight). Hold overhead. Time until arm buckles or drifts out of vertical.

safety_gates.block_body: A diagnosed rotator-cuff tear needs a rehab pathway, not a mobility program. Return once cleared for overhead loading.
Recent dislocation requires clinician clearance and typically capsule-stability work before overhead ROM work is safe.
Cervical radicular symptoms need their own workup. Overhead ROM work can amplify a nerve-root irritation.
Loss of range in every direction, including passively, is the pattern of adhesive capsulitis. Our own guidance is that it needs a separate rehab protocol — this program isn't it.

safety_gates.block_title: End-range work can stir that up
safety_gates.block_body: That location suggests the AC joint, and end-range overhead flexion can amplify it. You can still run this — but stop the session if that spot sharpens, and get it looked at if it doesn't settle.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll stop the session if that spot sharpens.

safety_gates.block_title: Worth finding out which it is
safety_gates.block_body: 'Unsure' usually means there's pain and nobody has looked at it. This programme is mobility work, not rehab — run it if you like, but if the pain is reproducible in the same position every time, get it assessed rather than stretching into it.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll get it assessed if it's reproducible.

safety_gates.block_title: This programme loads the range that hurts
safety_gates.block_body: You told us the last 30 degrees of overhead reach is painful. Every phase of this programme works exactly that range — passive, then active, then loaded. Get the shoulder assessed first; that's a better use of the next four weeks than training into it.

safety_gates.block_title: Watch that range as you load it
safety_gates.block_body: Occasional end-range discomfort is common and isn't a reason to stop you. It is a reason to hold the loaded progressions until the passive range is comfortable, and to stop a session on sharp pain rather than working through it.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll hold the loaded work if it sharpens.

safety_gates.block_body: If range is dropping in every direction and you're not sure why, that is worth a proper look before you start a mobility programme — adhesive capsulitis follows its own timeline and stretching into it does not shorten it.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll get it looked at if range keeps dropping.

safety_gates.block_title: Watch that spot as you load overhead
safety_gates.block_body: If you're not sure whether the pain is at the AC joint, note where it is next time it appears. End-range overhead flexion can amplify an irritated AC joint — stop the session if that exact spot sharpens.
safety_gates.acknowledge_label: Understood — I'll stop if that spot sharpens.

phases.name: Kinematic base · Weeks 1–3
phases.goal: Build passive ROM + scap sequencing before we add load.
phases.rationale: Ludewig 2000/2009 — scap upward-rotation lag is the kinematic pattern most consistently ASSOCIATED with rotator cuff-related shoulder pain (the condition older sources call 'impingement'); joint tightness alone explains it poorly. Association, not cause: the sequencing is what the evidence supports, and it is what this base phase trains.

phases.name: Active + light-loaded · Weeks 4–7
phases.goal: Add active ROM + light loaded overhead. Sotts press, TGU, empty bar OHS.
phases.rationale: Engineering choice, not a cited finding — we sequence cuff activation before end-range loading so the pattern is built under stress rather than reaching end-range cold. No cited paper establishes that ordering: Reinold et al. 2007 is an EMG comparison of three cuff exercises in asymptomatic subjects and reports nothing about loading order.

phases.name: Load + retest · Weeks 8–10
phases.goal: Consolidate loaded ROM. Retest at week 10.
phases.rationale: Karni 1998, Walker 2003 — consolidation with daily short sessions. Retest via shoulder-flexion goniometer + empty-bar OHS depth.

blocks.name: Thoracic prep · daily
blocks.note: Wall slides, foam-roller extensions, KB arm-bar. Prepares scap-thoracic mobility before shoulder work.

blocks.name: Scap activation
blocks.note: Band pull-apart variants, prone Y/T/W. Wake up lower trap + serratus so upward rotation happens before elevation.

blocks.name: Passive shoulder flexion
blocks.note: PVC pass-throughs, supine Sotts hold with light weight, wall-facing arm raises. Rib cage stays down.

blocks.name: Active shoulder flexion
blocks.note: Wall walks (from Handstand Walk drill library), face-away wall slides, half-kneeling reach. Active rotator-cuff engagement required.

blocks.name: Loaded overhead
blocks.note: Snatch-grip Sotts press · KB bottoms-up press · Turkish get-up. Load stays sub-maximal; ROM is the metric, not the number.

blocks.name: Overhead endurance
blocks.note: TGU hold (30s each side, working up), overhead KB carry, snatch balance.

blocks.name: Daily reset · pre-bed
blocks.note: 3 min of thoracic + shoulder pass-throughs at bedtime. Grease the pattern; sleep does the consolidation (Walker 2003).

weekly_template.note: Multi-dimensional generation. Each block declares a capability_slot; composeSlotDrills fills items[] from drill_library at the user's estimated level, attaching an external-focus cue (Wulf & Shea 2002). Contextual interference applies from Week 3+ (Shea & Morgan 1979 · Wulf & Shea 2002).

retest_metrics.display_name: Overhead squat depth (hip crease vs top of knee)
Turkish get-up hold time (best of L / R)

immediate_actions.action: Measure supine shoulder flexion — record baseline
Wall-slide test video (optional) — watch for scap dyskinesis pattern

physiological_targets.confidence: realistic for Foundation and Progression; stretch for Push (structural ROM limits)

push.confidence: fair — structural ROM begins to dominate near 190°

session_rationale.why_scap_first: Ludewig & Cook 2000, Ludewig & Reynolds 2009 — altered scapular upward-rotation timing is observed alongside impingement symptoms; how much of the subacromial space it drives is established by neither paper. Corrected 2026-09-05: this read "the dominant driver of subacromial space", a causal-magnitude claim in neither abstract, and one that contradicts the association-only framing this same file uses in its scap_first_shoulder_second rule and its phase 1 rationale. Sequencing scapular work before load is an engineering choice consistent with that association.
session_rationale.why_daily_short: Karni 1998, Walker 2003 consolidation — motor patterns require inter-session sleep for stabilisation. 10 min daily > 45 min biweekly.
session_rationale.why_load_early: Reinold, Escamilla and Wilk 2009 (JOSPT 39(2):105-117, PMID 19194023, a narrative review the authors grade Level of Evidence 5, and a different paper from the reinold_2007 EMG record cited in this programme) catalogued rotator-cuff EMG activation across a wide range of common drills; many light-load and banded variants produced cuff activation greater than typical bodyweight drills at comparable positions. Light load in Phase 2 leverages that catalogue to bias cuff engagement earlier. This is an engineering read of an EMG review, not an RCT of light-load vs bodyweight for shoulder-mobility outcome — see engineering_choices_flagged.
session_rationale.why_external_focus_cues: Wulf 1998, 2013 — external-focus cues (reach the ceiling) outperform internal (contract your lats) for motor retention.

engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: No RCT specifies the exact duration for shoulder-mobility work in athletes. Karni/Walker consolidation lit supports weekly re-testing over several weeks; 10 weeks is engineering.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Sotts press as primary loaded-overhead drill
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Coaching consensus in the weightlifting community. Not RCT'd against alternatives (KB press variants) for shoulder-mobility outcome specifically.
Historical / anecdotal (Pavel Tsatsouline lineage). Reproducible + measurable, but not RCT-validated as a shoulder-mobility outcome. We use it as a proxy for overhead endurance.
Widely used in weightlifting warm-ups; no dedicated RCT.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Supine flexion goniometer as primary retest
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: Kim 2013 documented supine flexion reliability; whether supine translates to loaded overhead is engineering inference — hence retest_metrics includes both supine AND OHS depth.

engineering_choices_flagged.choice: Light external load in Phase 2 to bias cuff activation early
engineering_choices_flagged.rationale: The cross-drill EMG catalogue is Reinold, Escamilla and Wilk 2009 (JOSPT 39(2):105-117), a Level-5 narrative review and not an RCT of light-load vs bodyweight for shoulder-mobility outcome; the reinold_2007 id in this programme resolves to a different paper, the 2007 J Athl Train EMG study. We treat the earlier-load bias as an engineering read of that catalogue.

contraindications: Diagnosed rotator-cuff tear (partial or full) — needs physio pathway
Recent shoulder dislocation / subluxation — capsule stability first
Cervical radicular symptoms into the arm — needs workup
Adhesive capsulitis (frozen shoulder) — separate rehab protocol
Active AC-joint irritation — end-range flexion can amplify
adaptive_engine_hooks: day_adjustment on symptom 'shoulder pain during flexion' → drop loaded_overhead this session; scap + thoracic only
amber week (≥3 amber shoulder symptom days) → skip loaded_overhead for a full week
phase_end evaluator: retest goniometer + OHS depth → tier promotion if targets hit

references.title: Alterations in shoulder kinematics and associated muscle activity in people with symptoms of shoulder impingement
references.used_for: Altered scap kinematics observed alongside impingement symptoms (the paper's own term); foundational rationale for scap-first sequencing. Association, not a demonstrated pathway.

references.title: The association of scapular kinematics and glenohumeral joint pathologies
references.used_for: Scap upward-rotation lag correlates with symptomatic impingement; drives phase-1 emphasis

references.authors: Reinold MM, Macrina LC, Wilk KE, Fleisig GS, Dun S, Barrentine SW, Ellerbusch MT, Andrews JR
references.title: Electromyographic analysis of the supraspinatus and deltoid muscles during 3 common rehabilitation exercises
references.used_for: This id now resolves to the EMG study, J Athl Train 42(4):464-469, PMID 18174934: 22 asymptomatic subjects, three isolated cuff exercises, no difference among them for supraspinatus. The cross-drill activation catalogue this programme actually described is a different work, Reinold, Escamilla and Wilk, JOSPT 2009;39(2):105-117, PMID 19194023, a narrative review the authors grade Level of Evidence 5; it needs its own citation id before Phase 2 copy can cite it. Neither paper states that cuff activation must precede end-range loading, so the light-load bias is an engineering choice, as this programme's own engineering_choices_flagged block already says. Corrected 2026-09-05: the record was dated 2007 at JOSPT 37(11):659-670, a locator with zero results, for a paper published in 2009, and a hard rule was attributed to text that is in neither abstract.

references.title: Kinematics and joint moments during the press to handstand
references.used_for: Shoulder-moment analysis for the straight-arm press to handstand — informs the no-heavy-load-early rule. Attribution flagged for founder review (see citations.json review_note): DOI resolves to a Mizutori-authored floor study; the 3× BW figure is a parallel-bars finding, not a floor finding. Terav uses this only for the general 'heavy shoulder moment early is unsafe' principle, not for a specific numeric threshold. CORRECTED 2026-09-05: the byline said Sadowski and no such paper exists, but the DOI was always right and resolves to Mizutori et al. It is a FLOOR study, not parallel bars, and the 3x bodyweight figure lived in its introduction quoting someone else. Its real finding — less-skilled performers produced LARGER shoulder flexion moments — supports this rule better than the withdrawn number.

references.authors: Walker MP, Brakefield T, Seidman J, Morgan A, Hobson JA, Stickgold R
references.title: Sleep and the time course of motor skill learning
references.used_for: Sleep-dependent consolidation of a motor pattern: doubling the amount of initial finger-tapping training did not increase the overnight gain, which is what the daily-short rationale leans on. A laboratory keypress task, so its application to mobility drills is an engineering choice. Corrected 2026-09-05: the record kept the Nature paper's title and byline over this Learning & Memory locator; the correct record is Walker MP, Brakefield T, Seidman J, Morgan A, Hobson JA, Stickgold R, 'Sleep and the time course of motor skill learning', Learn Mem 10(4):275-284, PMID 12888546.

Principles derived from the study of simple skills do not generalize to complex skill learning

references.title: Contextual interference effects on the acquisition, retention, and transfer of a motor skill
references.used_for: Contextual interference in motor learning — blocked-first, random after

references.authors: Kibler WB, Ludewig PM, McClure PW, Michener LA, Bak K, Sciascia AD
references.title: Clinical implications of scapular dyskinesis in shoulder injury: the 2013 consensus statement from the Scapular Summit
references.used_for: This programme means Kibler WB & Sciascia A (2010), 'Current concepts: scapular dyskinesis', BJSM 44(5):300-305 (PMID 19996329, DOI 10.1136/bjsm.2009.058834) - a DIFFERENT paper from the one the id kibler_2013 now serves. That paper describes a scapular examination consisting of visual inspection of scapular position at rest and during dynamic humeral movement, objective posture measurement and scapular corrective manoeuvres, and concludes that scapular dyskinesis 'appears to be a non-specific response to a painful condition in the shoulder rather than a specific response to certain glenohumeral pathology'. Corrected 2026-09-05: two things. (1) The id collision: kibler_2013 was resolving to the 2010 paper in citations.json while first-strict-pullup and muscle-up described the 2013 Scapular Summit consensus. The canonical record now serves the 2013 consensus; the 2010 paper needs its own id before this reference resolves correctly, and this reference should keep verification_status 'unverified' until it does. (2) 'SICK scapula screening pattern' is withdrawn: that term does not appear in the retrieved 2010 abstract, and the full text was unreachable (BMJ interstitial, not in PMC), so it can be neither confirmed nor excluded. SICK scapula is a separately named syndrome from a different paper. The screen this programme runs stands as an engineering choice built on the 2010 examination description.

references.title: Reliability of shoulder ROM measurement in supine position
references.used_for: Supine flexion goniometer reliability — the retest_metric anchor

references.authors: Escamilla RF, Yamashiro K, Paulos L, Andrews JR
references.title: Shoulder muscle activity and function in common shoulder rehabilitation exercises
references.used_for: EMG-guided drill selection — informs scap-activation block content

references.authors: Bullock GS, Faherty MS, Ledbetter L, Thigpen CA, Sell TC
references.title: Shoulder range of motion and baseball arm injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
references.used_for: Systematic review and meta-analysis in prospectively followed baseball players: high-quality evidence that deficits in throwing-arm total rotational arc and internal rotation are associated with upper-extremity injury. Cited for the rotational-ROM construct, and it establishes that construct only as an injury-risk marker in throwers. Engineering choice: including a rotational component alongside supine flexion in the retest for a general, non-throwing overhead-mobility population is a coaching judgement; an injury association in throwers does not by itself establish that the retest is informative here. Does NOT support the thoracic-to-shoulder pathway; that rationale rests on Kim 2013 plus coaching consensus. Corrected 2026-09-05: the record described a 2019 paper on baseball throwing PERFORMANCE that does not exist; the real paper is the 2018 meta-analysis on arm INJURY, and the programme's url was a PubMed search query rather than a record.

references.authors: Manske RC, Meschke M, Porter A, Smith B, Reiman M
references.title: A randomized controlled single-blinded comparison of stretching versus stretching and joint mobilization for posterior shoulder tightness measured by internal rotation motion loss
references.used_for: Randomised single-blinded trial in 39 ASYMPTOMATIC college-age participants (7 men, 32 women) comparing a CROSS-BODY stretch alone against cross-body stretch plus posterior joint mobilisation, with internal-rotation motion loss as the outcome. The combined group gained more internal rotation, but the between-group difference was not statistically significant. Corrected 2026-09-05: this read 'sleeper stretch effectiveness for posterior capsule tightness'. The trial tested the cross-body stretch, not the sleeper stretch, and choosing between those two is precisely what the citation was meant to settle; the participants were asymptomatic rather than people with symptomatic posterior capsule tightness; and the difference it did find was not significant. Prescribing the sleeper stretch is an engineering choice with no trial behind it here. The verification_status 'verified' flag on this reference was wrong for this use and should read 'unverified' - note it is stripped by Zod and has no runtime meaning either way. The record's PubMed search-string url is replaced by PMID 23015927.

references.authors: DiFiori JP, Caine DJ, Malina RM
references.title: Wrist pain, distal radial physeal injury, and ulnar variance in the young gymnast
references.used_for: Wrist-tolerance considerations if program includes handstand-adjacent work

references.title: Injury prevention in women's gymnastics
references.used_for: Narrative review of injury prevention in women's artistic gymnastics. It offers a framework of thinking - prevention grounded in science and medicine plus intimate knowledge of the demands of the movement - and no protocol, no effect size and no comparison; the full text is paywalled. Corrected 2026-09-05: previously described as a 'skill-readiness assessment framework' informing prerequisite gating. It is not an assessment framework. The prerequisite gating in this programme is an engineering choice, and the paper's population (young elite female gymnasts) is far from adult users working on overhead position.

onboarding_steps.title: What Terav will and won't do here
onboarding_steps.body_md: Overhead Mobility is a supplement, not a shoulder rehab. If you have a diagnosed labrum, cuff, or biceps injury, work with a physio first. Terav sharpens a range you already have — it does not restore range you've lost to pathology.
